article_title: Node.js Pre-Announces October 21 Security Releases for 26.x, 24.x and 22.x With a Highest Severity of High, as 26.12.0 and 24.22.0 Ship

content_preview.title: Node.js Pre-Announces October 21 Security Releases for 26.x, 24.x and 22.x With a Highest Severity of High, as 26.12.0 and 24.22.0 Ship
content_preview.summary: Node.js says new 26.x, 24.x and 22.x releases will land on or shortly after October 21 to fix vulnerabilities, highest severity High; 26.12.0 and 24.22.0 shipped October 14.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Node.js project has announced that it will release new versions of the 26.x, 24.x and 22.x release lines on or shortly after Wednesday, October 21, 2026 to address security vulnerabilities, according to the [Node.js security advisory page](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases). The page states that "The highest severity issue fixed in the 26.x release line is HIGH." It gives the same statement for the 24.x and 22.x lines.

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (386 words, inside the 300-800 Briefing range) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Context sections. Appropriately hedged: it presents the advisory as a pre-notice and does not speculate about the vulnerabilities.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three sources are first-party (nodejs.org, the Node.js project's own security advisory and release notes) and are on the allowlist; no allowlist edits were needed. Read from disk snapshots: source-0.html.gz (advisory, HTTP 200, 2,543 chars of text), source-1.html.gz (v26.12.0 release notes, HTTP 200), source-2.html.gz (v24.22.0 release notes, HTTP 200); suspicious_patterns null for all three. The advisory snapshot is short, but that is because the page itself is a one-minute pre-notice (Reading Time 1 min), not a thin fetch. Live re-fetch via curl on 2026-10-17 returned byte-identical text (same 2,543 chars; Last Updated Oct 14, 2026) for the advisory and unchanged release notes (16,151 and 38,738 chars). Advisory: the Summary says the project 'will release new versions of the 26.x, 24.x, 22.x releases lines on or shortly after, Wednesday, October 21, 2026 in order to address security vulnerabilities'; Impact gives 'The highest severity issue fixed in the 26.x/24.x/22.x release line is HIGH' for each line; 'End-of-Life versions are always affected when a security release occurs'; Release Schedule, security policy and nodejs-sec mailing list are all present. No CVE ids, no vulnerability details, and no per-severity counts appear on the page, and the article invents none. The quoted 26.x sentence is verbatim (article merges the three per-line sentences correctly as 'the same statement'). Release notes 26.12.0 (dated 2026-10-14): Notable Changes are exactly two, both SEMVER-MINOR: 'throw on missing WebAssembly or RX support' (Paolo Insogna) and 'add websocketMask() and websocketUnmask()' to http (James M Snell); article quotes verbatim and attributes credit to Snell correctly. Release notes 24.22.0 (2026-10-14, 'Krypton' LTS): crypto.parsePKCS12(), 'add a generic MAC API', net.BoundSocket support ('support sending net.BoundSocket to threads and child processes'), sqlite StatementSync.prototype.close() and [Symbol.dispose] are all listed as SEMVER-MINOR Notable Changes under 24.22.0 and are not attributed to the wrong version. Article says 'several' additions and does not claim the list is exhaustive (24.22.0 has more notable items, e.g. perf_hooks, util.throttle). Weekday check: Oct 21, 2026 is a Wednesday, consistent with the source. Writing-time vs now: at writing time (submission 2026-10-17T11:17Z) and at review time (2026-10-17) the advisory is the identical pre-notice, last updated Oct 14; the October 21 releases have not shipped, so nothing in the article is stale. The wording 'on or shortly after' is preserved faithfully, and the article's 'What We Don't Know' states the exact day is not fixed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote and attribution traces to the three sources. The article says 'at the time of writing' the page names no vulnerabilities or CVEs, which is accurate and correctly time-scoped. Internal link /article/2026-08/06-nodejs-ships-twice-delayed-july-security-release-patching-11-cves-as-node-18-and-20-sit-fully-unpatched uses the correct singular form and resolves to an existing published article src/content/articles/2026-08/06-... .md; the claim 'July cycle slipped twice before shipping' matches that article's own title/summary ('Twice-Delayed', 'after two delays'). The advisory page itself links to the July 29, 2026 security release as the previous entry, consistent with 'July cycle'. Orphan-link diff: set of body URLs minus article.sources is empty and article.sources minus body URLs is empty (the internal link is a site path, not a source).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. The closing sentence suggesting readers review the release lines in use is mild and non-editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. The only recent Node.js article (2026-10/08, 26.11.0/26.11.1) covers different releases; no existing article covers the October 21 pre-announcement or 26.12.0/24.22.0.
recommendations: When the October 21 releases ship, the bot should file a follow-up article with the actual CVE list and severities rather than editing this one.

No clarification or correction is warranted now: the advisory is unchanged since writing. If the project delays the releases or updates the page before publication, a later follow-up (not a correction) is the appropriate mechanism since the article is accurately time-scoped.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean APPROVE. Sources are first-party, wording of the pre-announcement is faithfully preserved, nothing invented, release-note items correctly attributed, length within range, internal link valid.
